item: Deeper study — the devout daily reader (deeper_study)
angle: A veteran pastor's read of the person who already shows up. He is not looking to be motivated; he is looking not to be interrupted. Design the app as a study desk: the text open, the tools within arm's reach, the record kept, nothing talking.
thesis: This reader's home screen currently promises depth and then hides it. The arrival strip tells him "Commentary is open below, with Compare and the original languages" (i18n.ts:915), but the only persistent Greek/Hebrew control lives inside a section that renders nothing unless he has an active plan (HomeScreen.tsx:3235 gated by 3223-3225), his day-one screen is a plan funnel with no scripture in it at all (heroChapterRefs has floors for comfort and pastor_leader but not for him, HomeScreen.tsx:1302-1315), the same chapter is printed twice (open in the hero, collapsed again in Today's Study), and tapping "Read" on that second copy silently credits his plan day behind his back (handleRead, HomeScreen.tsx:754-755). Fix the promise, not the persona: put the two depth tools next to the reading, give him a chapter on day one, delete the duplicate, make completion deliberate and single, key commentary to what is actually open, and give the two moments that matter to a long-haul reader — a skipped day and a finished plan — an honest next step. Add no cards, no badges, no encouragement. IMPORTANT: the docs named in my brief (docs/PERSONA-RESEARCH-2026-09-10.md and the scratchpad rulings packet dw-rulings.md) are not on disk — I searched the repo and every scratchpad. Every move below traces to the rulings JSON supplied inline in my brief or to a file:line in the live code, never to a research line I could not read.
principles: Never explain a devout reader's own practice back to him. The Bible AI teaser ('Bible AI can break down Greek and Hebrew words…', BibleAIPromptSection.tsx:29-32) reads as a stranger describing his morning. It also self-destructs after one use, so it is an ad, not a feature.
Tools belong beside the text, not in a section below it. Compare is in the hero (HomeScreen.tsx:2603-2624); Gk/Heb is a thousand lines down (3235). One toolbar.
One chapter, printed once. The hero already has a chapter slider and pills for multi-chapter days (HomeScreen.tsx:2408-2470), so Today's Study is a second printing of what is already open.
Completion is a decision, not a side effect. Mark as read is the act; expanding a passage is not.

Be honest about what is AI. The curated set is eight sources over the same twenty chapters (src/data/commentary.ts); most days he gets one 'AI Insight'. Label it plainly and never dress it as a named commentator — a name is not evidence.
A skipped day is a small grief for this reader, not a streak problem. Name the day that is still there, offer it in one tap, never guilt him.
A finished plan is a real moment. Today the plan day clamps at totalDays (HomeScreen.tsx:885) and he re-reads the last chapter forever.
No weekly review. features.weeklyReview is false for this persona (persona-config.ts:396) and weekly-review-for-all was explicitly rejected — do not build it back in under another name.
Richer and clearer, never stripped. Everything here keeps the photo plate, the white paper panel, the Georgia upright serif and the editorial chrome; nothing is removed except a duplicate and an ad.

journey.day0: He taps 'I want to go deeper in the Word' in the sheet, is saved with source 'onboarding', and lands on Home. Today he lands on the hero funnel 'Choose your reading plan' plus a second plan card below it — two asks and no scripture. After: a rotating study chapter is already open in the paper panel with Compare and Gk/Heb live above it, and there is exactly one plan ask, below the reading.
journey.first_session: Chapter open on arrival, credit-free (the seed bypasses handleRead, HomeScreen.tsx:1441-1456). He taps a word, gets Greek, taps Go deeper, the AI answers with cross-references (persona-config.ts:418-420). He writes one line under the passage and taps Mark as read. Total taps to the text: zero.
journey.return_visit: 'Good morning, Ashley. Day 34.' (persona-config.ts:242-245). Hero eyebrow reads 'NEW TESTAMENT IN 90 DAYS — DAY 34'. Today's chapter is open. Commentary is already expanded under it. Nothing asks him for anything.
journey.week2: The Notes tab is now a study record — fourteen entries, each stamped with the chapter it came from, filterable by the Study tag. The reflection question has not repeated: a seven-question bank rotates by day index, so he is answering a new question rather than 'What stood out to you in today's reading?' for the fourteenth time.
journey.missed_day: He misses Tuesday. The plan advances on the calendar regardless (calcPlanDay, HomeScreen.tsx:124-140) and Tuesday's chapters are gone. After: one quiet line under the date strip — 'You're on Day 34. Day 33 is still there.' with 'Read Day 33', which sets the existing planDayOffset. No red dot, no badge, no apology asked of him. It disappears the moment he reads it or taps the ×.
journey.seasonal: Day 90 of the New Testament plan. The finish card fires once today (DoneCelebration with planFinish, HomeScreen.tsx:726) and then the plan clamps at Day 90 forever and serves him the same chapter every morning for the rest of his life. After: a Finished card takes the place of the plan reading — 'You finished the New Testament in 90 Days' with three real next steps and 'Read it again', and until he picks, the hero falls to the study floor rather than repeating.

comfort_access: Two doors, both already built, and one honest limit. The path swatch sits in the Home header for every persona and opens the one sheet in a tap; the comfort card there reads "I'm going through something hard — Comfort scriptures. Nothing else asked of you," which is the right sentence for a man who has read every morning for four years and this morning cannot. Saving it navigates him straight there, and the comfort path never asks him the once-only path question and never opts him into push. The limit worth naming to Ashley: a devout reader in grief will usually not re-declare himself; he will just stop opening the app. So the second door matters more — the Ask surface has to be able to hold a hard question without flinching, and it does (the selection toolbar's Ask AI and the gold button both carry the chapter he is in as context). Nothing else should be added: no "are you okay" prompts, no check-in cards, and never anything resembling the "Feeling Stronger?" graduation prompt, which is removed for good.
reminders: One notification a day at an hour he sets, and it tells the truth. Today the body names a chapter from a fixed forty-passage rotation on the server, which is not his plan — for a man on Day 34 of the New Testament that is small and grating. Carry the plan reference with the subscription (written from the plan passages the client already persists) and send "New Testament in 90 Days — Day 34. Romans 8 is ready." When the server does not know, fall back to "Your reading is ready" rather than naming the wrong book. Nothing else: no streak-at-risk push, no "you haven't read in three days", no second nudge. This reader does not need to be chased, and a chasing notification is the fastest way to make a four-year habit feel supervised. The reminder hour and the on/off switch stay where they are in Settings, and the calendar fallback stays for devices without push. Spanish and Portuguese templates are missing entirely — those are Claude-drafted and Ashley signs them off before they ship.
instrumentation: reading_complete — fires only from Mark as read, with the chapter. Today 'daily_reading' fires on expand, so nothing in the data distinguishes opening from reading. Add to the TRACKED_EVENTS allowlist in src/utils/analytics.ts:31-37.
daily_reading — keep, but it must never fire from the arrival seed. Assert that in the test: the seed calls loadPassage directly and must not route through handleRead.

commentary_open — the Home commentary card is currently untracked; only the note drawer's AI commentary fires trackBehavior('commentary') (VerseNoteDrawer.tsx:207). Without it you cannot tell whether the persona's headline feature is used.
commentary_source — which tab he lands on, curated vs 'AI Insight'. This is the number that says whether the curated twenty chapters are worth extending.
greek_hebrew — already fires on word tap (HomeScreen.tsx:1743) but not on the mode toggle. Fire on toggle too, so reachability can be measured before and after the tool row moves.
compare_on — no event today. If Compare is genuinely used, it earns its place in the tool row; if not, that is worth knowing.
catchup_read — the catch-up line was shown, and whether he took it. Proves whether a missed day is a real problem or a designer's assumption.
plan_finished / plan_started_after_finish — the pair that proves the finish card ends a dead end rather than ending a habit.
ai_prompt (exists) — watch the rate after the teaser card is removed. If it holds or rises, the teaser was an ad; if it falls, put a quieter entry back.
journal_save (exists) — entries per reader per week is the honest week-two retention measure for this persona, better than streak length.

Caveat to record: src/utils/behavior.ts:53 stamps events with a UTC date, so an Australian reading at 8am local is filed to the previous day. Do not use dw_behavior_v1 dates for any day-boundary claim; the plan/streak axis is local and must stay that way.
self_serve_levers: src/data/commentary.ts — a campus pastor or Ashley adds a chapter key under any of the eight named sources and it appears the next deploy. Today it is eight sources over the same twenty chapters, which is why most days fall to AI; this is the single highest-value content lever on this path. It is a bundled module, so the /books/* service-worker cache trap does not apply.

src/data/study.ts (new) — the day-one floor chapter rotation, a plain array of chapter references in exactly the shape src/data/pastor.ts:8 already uses. Editing the list changes what a plan-less study reader opens on, with no other code touched.

src/utils/persona-config.ts, deeper_study journal.prompts — the rotating reflection bank, as a list of i18n keys. Adding, removing or reordering questions is a one-line edit; the text itself lives with all the other copy in src/utils/i18n.ts, which is also where Spanish, Portuguese and Indonesian go.
src/utils/persona-config.ts, deeper_study journal.tags — the filter chips on the Notes tab for this path.

src/data/plans.ts — plans, their day-by-day passages and totalDays. Warning to carry: changing a plan id means rewiring four files (personalization.ts, SetupPromptModal.tsx, PlansScreen.tsx, PastorStudyOnboarding.tsx) or the wizard starts a dead plan. Adding or editing passages inside an existing id is safe.
netlify/functions/push-send.js — notification wording and the verse snippets, per language. Adding Spanish and Portuguese is a data edit in this one file; it is a deploy, not an admin screen.

In the app, for the reader himself: the path swatch in the Home header, the campus chip beside it, the reminder hour and push toggle in Settings, the translation strip and Compare and Gk/Heb on the reading, and Restart on any plan from the Plans tab.

Named honestly as NOT self-serve: persona sectionOrder, the milestone day lists (duplicated in two files with different values), the weekly-review question bank, the push cadence, and adding a campus. All of those are developer edits today.

open_decisions: The study floor chapter list — roughly thirty chapters for a reader who wants depth, in the shape of PASTOR_CHAPTERS. Ashley's pick, or Claude drafts a list and he strikes what he does not want. Nothing ships until he has seen it, because it becomes the first screen a plan-less study reader ever sees.

The seven reflection questions. I have drafted them plain and direct with no jargon; he approves the wording, or replaces the bank. If he would rather keep one fixed question, say so and the bank is dropped — the mechanism costs nothing either way.
The AI Insight honesty line. Mine reads 'Written by this app's AI for this chapter, not by a published commentator.' His call whether that sentence goes in, and in whose words.

Removing the plan-day credit from handleRead is a cross-persona change, not a deeper_study one: congregation and pastor_leader currently also get a day credited by expanding a passage. Fix it for everyone, or gate it to this path only?

The same duplicate-chapter redundancy exists for pastor_leader, which also renders plan_scripture over the same hero chapters. Fix it there in this pass, or leave the pastor home alone until he has seen this one?

The notification: add a plan reference column to push_subscriptions so it can name his actual chapter (a Supabase migration, kept in the repo, plus two small function edits), or leave the generic 'Your reading is ready' and stop naming a passage at all?
Spanish and Portuguese notification copy — Claude drafts, he signs off before it sends to a single Futuros phone.
The preview approval itself. One branch, one deploy-preview link, his eyes on the deeper_study home and on all five personas for the Sermon Notes move, before anything merges.
risks: This is cumulatively a reshape of the deeper_study home, which is exactly the class of change that was reverted on 1 September as 'completely stripped'. The defence is that every change here adds or relocates, and only two things are removed: a duplicate printing of the same chapter, and an advertisement. The photo plate, the paper panel, the Georgia serif, the commentary card and the editorial chrome all stay. Say that out loud on the preview.

The Sermon Notes demotion touches all five paths from one line of code. It is his own ruling, but it will be the most visible difference on four home screens, so it needs its own look on the preview rather than being folded in silently.

Removing the plan-day credit from handleRead changes what a completed day means. Anyone mid-plan who had been crediting days by expanding will see their plan stop advancing unless they tap Mark as read. That is the correct behaviour and it is what the code comment says was intended, but it is a behaviour change to a synced record and it should be called out, not slipped in.

Never rebuild dw_activeplans or any dw_* record from React state when writing the finished-plan flag — merge into what is in localStorage and touch only that field, or a second device's progress is overwritten by stale mount-time state.

The finished-plan change alters todaysPlanPassages, which is also written to dw_todays_plan_passages for the Study Notes tab and drives heroChapterRefs, the commentary list and the audio chain. Every one of those needs a live check, not just a build.

Push cannot be verified on a deploy preview — pushSupported allowlists futuresdailyword.com, www and localhost only. Verify the notification change on localhost or on production after merge, never on the preview link, and do not report it as tested from the preview.

Extending commentary coverage is the highest-value lever but it is real writing work: eight sources over twenty chapters today. If nobody writes more, the honesty line will be on screen most mornings. That is still better than the alternative, but he should decide it knowingly.
Adding i18n keys without the Spanish, Portuguese and Indonesian rows leaves t() returning the raw key on screen for Futuros readers. Every new key ships with all four languages in the same commit.

Home already carries hardcoded English beyond the toggle I am removing — 'ADDITIONAL READING' / "TODAY'S CHAPTERS" (HomeScreen.tsx:3453), 'Share' (3481), 'Add' (3502). Fixing them is a separate small pass; do not let it expand this one.
